title: Moving customers to a Net term writes a row with no limit line
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop moves the three customers on a term of its own to Net 45, and you check the history.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The shop's own term {Term-A}, due 20 days after the invoice date, is held by exactly three customers.
    For example: {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S12-09 N20 and its customers are ZZAUTOTEST S12-09 Alpha, Bravo and Charlie.
  • Starting screen: the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "⋯" at the right of the {Term-A} row.
  2. Click "Move Customers".
  3. Choose "Net 45" in "Move To".
  4. Click "Move 3 Customers".
  5. Click the "⋯" page menu beside "New Credit Term".
  6. Click "Audit Log".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the menu opens.
  • Step 2: the window opens with 3 selected.
  • Step 3: the dropdown shows Net 45.
  • Step 4: a green success toast shows.
  • Step 5: the menu opens.
  • Step 6: the newest row reads Event "Customers moved" and Details "3 customers from {Term-A} to Net 45", with no credit-limit line.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11681 (Story 12, Credit Terms audit log)

  • S12-R3 table, customers moved: “Customers are moved (Story 4: Move Customers) | "Customers moved" | "{n} customers from {from} to {to}" ("1 customer from {from} to {to}" for one), followed by "Credit limit set to $0 (previous limits are in each customer's note)" when the target is COD or Credit Hold”
  • Key Decisions: “Every change on the Credit Terms page is recorded in an organization-wide Credit Terms Log (Story 12: Credit Terms audit log), and every customer moved by Move Customers also gets a note naming the old term, the new term and the user.”
